title: The Domestic Weather Memory Era
summary: A short-lived domestic design movement that taught everyday objects to store weather, mood, and the private history of sheltering together.

title: The room rains back
body: The canopy opens with a sigh. A gentle rain falls upward toward the ceiling, carrying the scent of a childhood hallway and a voice calling everyone inside before the thunder.

title: The forecast forgets your name
body: You leave the clasp untouched. By morning, every forecast shows clear skies where you stand, as if the atmosphere has politely removed you from its memory.

title: The Umbrella That Remembers Every Storm
accessionNote: Donated by the last household insured against emotional weather.
summary: A translucent umbrella stores traces of every storm beneath which it was opened, preserving rain, voices, and the feeling of having somewhere to return.
artifactLabel: Silver droplets hang motionless beneath the canopy. Along the handle, tiny brass dates mark storms that official weather archives insist never occurred.
visualDescription: A translucent umbrella is displayed open above a dark pedestal. Suspended silver droplets glow beneath its canopy, and rows of tiny dates are engraved into its brass handle.

title: The Counterfactual Communications Boom
summary: An optimistic communications age when public telephone networks briefly connected callers to plausible lives they had chosen not to live.

title: A familiar stranger answers
body: The voice knows your laugh but not your name. Behind it, dishes clatter in a kitchen you almost recognize, and someone asks whether the train was worth missing.

title: A missed call arrives from you
body: The receiver stays quiet. Seconds later, the telephone records a missed call from your own number, dated eleven years from now and marked: Do not apologize.

title: The Telephone for Calling Roads Not Taken
accessionNote: Seized from Platform Zero after the counterfactual network shutdown.
summary: A cream rotary telephone once connected callers to lives formed by decisions they nearly made, charging each conversation in certainty rather than coins.
artifactLabel: Its dial has no numbers, only choices: stay, leave, speak, wait. A second receiver rests behind the first, warm despite never being lifted.
visualDescription: A cream rotary telephone sits inside a glass case. Words instead of numbers circle its dial, and a second receiver rests behind it with a faint amber glow.
